summary: Zutphen (Gelderland) charges for street and lot parking under a municipal parking-tax ordinance. The council adopted the 2026 version on 15 December 2025, in force from 1 January 2026. It sets hourly rates of 3.10 euros at locations such as Groenmarkt, Nieuwstad and Stationsplein and 2.50 euros at others such as Brasseroord, Martinetsingel and Noorderhaven, which is 5 to 10 cents above 2025. Vispoortplein/Houtwal, Roodsplein, Isendoornstraat and Molengracht-west cost 1.95 euros per hour or 11.55 euros per day, and the Houtwal lot behind the police station 1.05 euros per hour or 3.20 euros per day. A resident permit costs 198.60 euros a year, and the ordinance sets the costs of an additional assessment for unpaid parking tax at 82 euros. Council and executive papers from 2022 and 2023 (dates taken from file metadata) state an intention to reduce inner-city parking sharply, with three large car parks at the edge (Station, Polsbroek, Houtwal); they report no vote. A May 2025 Burgerbelang amendment to the draft Omgevingsvisie proposed stimulating parking garages within or at the edge of the centre and cited about 500 spaces in and around the centre; its vote was not found. The national parking register, read on 21 October 2026, lists the NS-operated P+R Lijmerij by the station with 375 spaces and old (June 2021) tariffs of 1.62 euros per hour or 8.11 euros per day, while its live feed reports a capacity of 308, so the figures conflict. Public charging is being expanded through collective traffic decisions in 2023 and 2025 that designate charge-only bays, with the second bay at most locations applying only once a post reaches 1,750 kWh a year. The municipal website was unavailable on 21 October 2026, so official parking pages and paid-parking hours could not be read.

items.text: The Zutphen council adopted the Verordening parkeerbelastingen 2026 on 15 December 2025 (proposal from the executive dated 18 November 2025); it repeals the 2025 ordinance and applies from 1 January 2026. Article 9 sets the costs of an additional assessment for unpaid parking tax (naheffingsaanslag) at 82.00 euros; the ordinance does not say whether the unpaid parking tax is added to that amount.

The 2026 tariff table (in force from 1 January 2026) sets hourly rates of 3.10 euros at locations including Groenmarkt, Hagepoortplein, Laarstraat, Nieuwstad, Stationsplein and Zaadmarkt, and 2.50 euros at locations including Brasseroord, IJsselkade, Martinetsingel, Noorderhaven and Rozengracht. The table does not itself classify locations as core or fringe.

The 2026 table gives long-stay lots a cheaper rate: Vispoortplein/Houtwal, Roodsplein, Isendoornstraat and Molengracht-west cost 1.95 euros per hour with a day ticket of 11.55 euros, and the Houtwal lot behind the police station costs 1.05 euros per hour or 3.20 euros per day. A motorhome bay on that lot costs 14.80 euros per day.

The 2025 ordinance (council decision of 16 December 2024, in force from 1 January 2025) charged 3.00 euros per hour at the locations that cost 3.10 in 2026 (for example Groenmarkt, Hagepoortplein, Laarstraat, Nieuwstad, Stationsplein, Zaadmarkt) and 2.40 euros where 2026 has 2.50. Vispoortplein/Houtwal, Roodsplein, Isendoornstraat and Molengracht-west cost 1.90 euros per hour (day ticket 11.15 euros), and the Houtwal lot behind the police station 1.00 euro per hour or 3.10 euros per day. The 2026 table raised these rates by 5 to 10 cents per hour (day tickets to 11.55 and 3.20 euros). A Houtmarkt entry at 2.90 euros per hour in 2025 does not appear in the 2026 table.
items.source_title: Verordening parkeerbelastingen gemeente Zutphen 2025 (decision of 16 December 2024, with tariff table 2025)

items.text: Under the 2026 tariff table an annual resident permit for parking on a bay for permit holders (belanghebbendenplaats) costs 198.60 euros (192.00 euros in 2025), a second resident permit 321.60 euros, a business permit 649.80 euros and a visitor pass 40.05 euros per month. Annual subscriptions for the pay-and-display lots run from 232.80 euros (Houtwal behind the police station) through 389.40 euros (Vispoortplein/Houtwal, Roodsplein, Isendoornstraat, IJsselkade) up to 1,142.40 euros (Spittaalstraat, Laarstraat, Donkere Steeg, Nieuwstad, Rijkenhage/Hagepoortplein); market-stall holders pay less (48.60 to 163.80 euros) at three lots.

The 2026 cost decision for parking fines (adopted by the council on 15 December 2025) estimates 2,600 fines at a calculated cost of 123.56 euros each (total costs 321,265 euros; the table is labelled 2025 costs). The fine set in the ordinance is 82 euros, so this is an enforcement-cost estimate, not a usage statistic.

The P+R car park next to Zutphen station (Noorderhaven district) was reported as newly completed in March 2017, with 375 car spaces and more than 600 bicycle spaces; it was designed by MoederscheimMoonen Architects, with Continental Car Parks among the contractors.
items.source_title: P+R Car Park Zutphen / MoederscheimMoonen Architects (ArchDaily)

items.text: Read on 21 October 2026: the national parking register (RDW NPR open data) lists P+R Lijmerij (Zutphen, Lijmerij 2) with Nederlandse Spoorwegen as operator, 375 spaces, a 2.1 m height limit and 24/7 opening, at 1.62 euros per hour or 8.11 euros per day. The capacity, tariff and opening entries in this static record carry start dates of 14 to 15 June 2021, so they are old and may be out of date. The live status feed for the same facility, read the same day, reports a parking capacity of 308 (249 vacant), not 375, so the register's two capacity figures conflict; a 2017 architecture write-up also gives 375.
items.source_title: RDW Open Parkeerdata (NPR): P+R Lijmerij (Zutphen), static and dynamic feed

items.text: A framework note for the 2023-2026 inner-city programme (PDF created 15 May 2023 according to its file metadata; the text reports no adoption or vote) states the aim that the number of car parking places in the inner city is to be reduced substantially ('fors teruggebracht'), with three large car parks at the edge of the inner city as the starting point, and that visitors are to be directed as far as possible to the three central car parks at the Station, Polsbroek and Houtwal.

A Zutphen executive (college) paper listing seven priority mobility measures (PDF created 19 January 2022 according to its file metadata; the text carries no decision date) says the municipality wants to abolish about 23 parking places in characteristic parts of the inner city, mostly permit-holder places and a few paid ones (disabled bays stay), is working towards merging permit and regular parking, wants about 280 bicycle spaces at the edges of the core shopping area, and plans a better walking route from the Houtwal car park to the inner city, with execution given as 2022-2023. Whether these were carried out is not confirmed.
items.source_title: Toelichting op de maatregelen uitvoeringsplan (college, Zutphen)

items.text: On 26 May 2025 councillor Marloes Roerdink (Burgerbelang) submitted amendment 2025-A0012 to the draft Omgevingsvisie. It would replace 'three central parking facilities around the inner city' with a network of parking facilities at strategic locations, have the municipality facilitate and stimulate parking garages within or at the edge of the centre, and reduce on-street spaces step by step only after replacements exist. The amendment itself states that Zutphen currently has about 500 parking places in and around the centre. This is a proposal; the council vote on it was not found.

On 12 June 2023 the executive (college of mayor and aldermen) designated charge-only bays near 10 new public charge posts (for example Emmerikseweg 252, Jan Rozeboomstraat 32, Oranjelaan 24). Two bays are designated at each location, but for nine of the ten (all except David Evekinkstraat 7) the second bay applies only once the post uses at least 1,750 kWh a year; the decision lapses for a location not carried out by 30 June 2025. The decision cites a forecast that about 424 charge points would be needed in 2025 and an agreement with a charge operator, and notes that 17 proactive posts had been approved in two 2022 decisions.
items.source_title: Gemeenteblad 2023, 254704: aanwijzen parkeerplaatsen voor opladen elektrisch voertuig (verzamelbesluit)

items.text: A collective traffic decision by the executive (dated 26 May 2025, published 28 May 2025) designates two charge-only bays near each of 27 listed locations (for example Bakerstraat 14, Braamkamp 103, 's Gravenhof 14, Het Glacis 23). For all locations except David Evekinkstraat 3 and 's Gravenhof 14, the second bay applies only once a post reaches 1,750 kWh a year. David Evekinkstraat 3, 's Gravenhof 14 and Het Glacis 23 get an extra sign saying a parking permit or ticket is required. The decision lapses for a location not carried out by 31 May 2027.
items.source_title: Gemeenteblad 2025, 231109: aanwijzen parkeerplaatsen voor opladen elektrisch voertuig (verzamelbesluit)

items.text: The municipal policy rule on charge posts and charging on public land (Beleidsregel oplaadpalen en opladen op openbaar terrein 2024) has been in force since 22 August 2024 and replaces earlier rules.
items.source_title: Beleidsregel oplaadpalen en opladen op openbaar terrein gemeente Zutphen 2024 (CVDR723808)

gaps: https://www.zutphen.nl (parking, permits, zone maps, Omgevingsvisie and Polsbroek PDFs) showed a 'tijdelijk niet bereikbaar' maintenance page on 21 October 2026, so paid-parking hours, the current zone map and the Polsbroek spatial framework (April 2024) could not be read.
Paid-parking hours (Parkeerverordening Zutphen 1991 / permit regulation 2019) not found in a source I could open; third-party claims of Monday-Saturday 08-18 and Friday to 21 were not used.
Outcome of the council vote on amendment 2025-A0012 and the adopted Omgevingsvisie text not found; no 2026 council paper on the tariff increase or on new garages found.

No De Stentor, RTV Oost or other regional press article on Zutphen parking could be found or opened; WebSearch budget ran out, so press coverage, the Mobiliteitsvisie Binnenstad 2018 and the parking implementation plan (parkeervisie) remain unread.

No occupancy, usage or visitor statistics for the centre car parks found; the number of spaces in the Station, Polsbroek and Houtwal lots is not stated in sources read (only the amendment's 'about 500 places in and around the centre').
NS pages for P+R Lijmerij (ns.nl) are script-rendered and gave no readable tariff text; P+R tariff comes only from the RDW NPR record, whose entries date from June 2021 and may be outdated.
https://www.world-architects.com/de/architecture-news/works/pandr-parking returned a Cloudflare block (403) and was not used.
Gelre Ziekenhuizen car park (Q-Park, 250 spaces) appears in the RDW NPR but its record expired in 2022; not used.
